Hi Clara / Ben,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the candid walkthrough of where SearchGrid wants to use summarization + policy classification in the agent workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- What we heard: high volume (5–10k queries/day), median input length ~600 tokens, 8–10% of queries hit policy-sensitive flags requiring redaction/safety classification before presenting downstream.
- Priority: keep 95th-pct latency under 300ms for single-turn suggestions, and maintain high recall on policy triggers (want to avoid false negatives).
- Immediate ask: we need a sample prompt set (real user queries, edge cases, and examples that should be redacted) so we can run a short eval and provide model + quantization recommendations.

Attaching a short demo notes PDF and a CSV template (prompt-sample-template.csv) to make the intake easier — please fill with representative queries, mark which should be redacted or flagged (column: expected_action).

On our side well run a fast-turn model-fit evaluation and follow up with: recommended model family, a simple benchmark (latency / cost / quality tradeoffs), and suggested prompt patterns + redaction guidance.

Proposed timeline:
- You send sample prompts + redaction examples (CSV) — target by Tue (2 business days)
- We run eval & return model shortlist + benchmark summary — within 4 business days after receiving samples

Next steps: can you confirm who will own the prompt export and whether we should expect PII in the samples (if yes, well provide a redaction checklist)?

Thanks,
Mateo

Hi Clara / Ben — copying Marissa from our eval team. Short answers + a checklist we can use to minimize back-and-forth.

1) Eval deliverables (what you'll get):
- Model shortlist (3 candidates) with recommended quantization profiles
- Benchmark table: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens-per-second throughput, per-1000-token cost estimate, policy-flag precision/recall on your labeled samples
- Prompt templates: canonical prompt + guardrails for redaction + example few-shot seeds
- Regression risk notes: tests we run to detect quality regressions on future model swaps (simple eval harness + snapshot of prompts)

2) Quick model guidance based on call:
- If you prioritize recall on policy flags (and can accept slightly higher cost): recommend larger dense model variant on dedicated nodes (wed propose rwi-large-1, see attached brief).
- If low cost + sub-200ms median latency is the priority: rwi-medium-quantized (8-bit) on Dedicated with prefix caching and 2x batching is likely the best trade.
- Well provide a numerical tradeoff in the benchmark report once we have your prompt samples.

3) Redaction checklist (short):
- Remove direct identifiers where possible (names, SSNs, emails) OR replace with consistent tokens (e.g., <NAME_1>).
- Mark rows where manual review is required (column: manual_review=true).
- For policy-sensitive examples, include the expected label (columns: expected_action: keep|flag|redact).
- If you cant redact certain fields due to reproducibility, mark them and well treat them as sensitive in our eval and segregate them from shared pendings.

4) Prompt sample guidance (CSV columns in template):
- id, raw_user_text, context_notes, expected_action, expected_classification_labels, priority
- Capture edge cases (long-form concatenated logs, non-English snippets, obfuscated profanity, partially redacted PII) — these help surface model weaknesses.

5) Benchmarks & example links:
- Raw throughput/latency baseline well use: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/benchmarks/searchgrid/text-gen-benchmarks-202705.csv
- Example prompt template doc: https://docs.redwood.inference/collections/prompt-sample-template

Attachments: rw-model-recs-brief.pdf (contains brief performance expectations and configuration options).

Next steps: once you upload the CSV template filled with at least 300 representative rows (mix of normal + edge cases), well queue a 72-hour eval run and share a detailed recap. If you prefer, we can run an initial smoke test on 30 rows within 24 hours to sanity check redaction mapping.

Cc: Marissa — can you confirm the eval queue ETA for 300 rows?

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
